newsitem.title: USA: Tennessee lawmakers approve $14.5 billion budget.
newsitem.headline: Tennessee lawmakers approve $14.5 billion budget.

text.p: The Tennessee Legislature ended its annual session on Saturday after approving a $14.5 billion budget that contains no tax increases or new taxes.

The final version draws only $43 million from the Tennessee Housing Development Agency's reserves to balance the budget, a figure lawmakers said would allow the agency to keep low-income housing programs intact.
Gov. Don Sundquist had proposed drawing $88 million from that fund to offset revenue shortfalls.
The budget eliminates 1,400 state jobs. About half of those jobs were already vacant, and all but 244 of the affected employees have been moved to other posts.
The budget includes a 1.5 percent raise for state employees and increases public school spending by $200 million.
It relies on a 6 percent tuition increase for state colleges and universities, which still must be approved by the university system.
Lawmakers tabled until next year a proposal to privatize the state's prisons. Lawmakers also delayed action until next year on a proposed constitutional amendment to establish a state lottery.
In the final moments, the House also approved a $20.1 million bond bill for local projects in Memphis, Knoxville, Chattanooga and Johnson City. It had already been approved in the Senate.

Funding for the projects was part of a deal last year that led to approval of $55 million in state funding for construction of Nashville's new stadium for the Houston Oilers. The bond bill passed last year but had to be approved again to correct a glitch in the language.
